sources: Penn State Extension, Cluster Flies: "These flies are not reproducing within the structure, but become active on warm days and crawl out of wall voids and attics in a confused attempt to go back outside."; "the flies will gather in large numbers at windows within the home on warm winter days. The flies are typically sluggish in flight"; "Although insecticidal dust treatments to these voids may kill thousands of flies..."; https://extension.psu.edu/cluster-flies

Colorado State University Extension, Cluster Flies and Other Winter Flies: "Cluster flies found in buildings are in a dormant state and cannot reproduce indoors."; "Cluster flies develop by feeding on earthworms."; "cluster flies then find sheltered areas in wall voids or attics where they may aggregate"; https://extension.colostate.edu/resource/cluster-flies-and-other-winter-flies/
title: Why Thousands of Flies Wake Up in Your House Walls 🪰 (Things Living In Your House)
tiktok_caption: why are there so many flies in my house 🪰 cluster flies spend winter in your attic and wall voids, then crawl out on warm days. They can't breed indoors: their babies grow inside earthworms. Ever had a winter fly invasion? #clusterflies #flysinhouse #winterpests #meatballmyths

beats.say: Thousands of flies can sleep inside your walls.
One warm day wakes them. They crawl out.
They crowd your sunny windows, dazed and sluggish.
They can't breed in your house.
Their babies grow inside earthworms, outdoors.
They're just lost, not nesting. Right now,
